reviews.notes: Krishna recounts primordial transmission of Yoga to Vivasvan (Sun god), then Manu, then Ikshvaku.
Transmission through royal sages (rājarṣayaḥ) and subsequent decay of the ancient lineage over time.
Krishna reveals this supreme secret Yoga anew to Arjuna because he is a loyal devotee and beloved friend.
Arjuna chronological question: how could Krishna have taught Vivasvan who lived ages earlier in time?
Krishna explains the reality of multiple births: I remember them all, whereas thou rememberest them not.
Divine incarnation doctrine: unborn, imperishable Lord taking birth through his own creative power (Maya).
Celebrated avatar declaration: whenever righteousness declines and evil rises, I manifest Myself.
Purpose of divine descent: protecting the virtuous, destroying evildoers, and restoring dharma age after age.
Whoso comprehends the truth of Krishna divine birth and work transcends rebirth, merging into His being.
Many seekers, purified by the austerity of wisdom and freed from passion, fear, and wrath, attain divine union.
Universal responsiveness: in whatever way men approach Me, so do I welcome them; all paths lead to Me.
Men worship lesser deities seeking swift worldly fruit, which readily materializes in this mortal realm.
Creation of the four orders (cāturvarṇyam) based on innate qualities and duties; God is author yet non-doer.
Works do not contaminate the Lord because He harbors no craving for fruits; knowing this frees from karmic bondage.
Ancient seekers after liberation acted with this understanding; Arjuna is urged to follow their venerable footsteps.
The paradox of action and inaction that confuses even sages; Krishna promises to expound saving knowledge.
Necessity to distinguish lawful action, prohibited action (vikarma), and inaction (akarma); deep is the path.
Highest insight: he who discerns inaction in action, and action in inaction, is truly wise among humans.
The sage whose enterprises are devoid of selfish intent has his works consumed in the fire of wisdom.
Renouncing fruit of action, ever content, and independent, one remains inactive in spirit even while acting.
Free from yearning, self-controlled, relinquishing greed, performing mere bodily functions without guilt.
Content with whatever chance brings, transcending dualities, free from envy, equal in success and failure.
The work of an unattached, liberated soul whose consciousness is anchored in wisdom melts away wholly.
All is Brahman: the ladle, the oblation, the fire, the offerer, and the goal of him who meditates on Brahman.
Survey of sacrifices: some offer worship to the gods; others offer sacrifice into the flame of Brahman.
Ascetics who offer the senses into the fire of restraint, and others who offer sense-objects into sense-fires.
Yogins offering all vital and sensory actions into the fire of self-discipline kindled by wisdom.
Variety of seekers: offering wealth, penance, yogic disciplines, silent scriptural study, and knowledge.
Pranayama disciplines: pouring inhalation into exhalation and exhalation into inhalation to still breath.
Those who fast strictly offering life-breaths into life-breaths; all such offerings purge the taint of sin.
Partakers of the immortal sacrificial remnants attain eternal Brahman; without sacrifice neither world is won.
Diverse sacrifices spread before Brahman; recognizing them as products of action brings liberation.
The sacrifice of wisdom is superior to material oblations, for all action finds its consummation in knowledge.
Approach the seers of truth with reverence, earnest inquiry, and humble service to receive divine instruction.
Endowed with truth, you will never fall back into delusion, beholding all creatures in the Self and in Me.
Even the greatest sinner can cross over all ocean of transgression upon the reliable bark of spiritual wisdom.
As blazing flame reduces fuel to ashes, so the fire of knowledge (jñānāgniḥ) burns all works to ash.
No purifier exists comparable to wisdom; the person perfected in Yoga realizes it naturally within in due time.
The person endowed with faith, dedication, and sensory mastery secures knowledge and swiftly wins supreme peace.
The ignorant, faithless, and doubt-ridden soul is ruined; neither this world, nor heaven, nor joy awaits the doubter.
Actions cannot bind one who has renounced works through Yoga, severed doubts by wisdom, and possesses the Self.
Concluding call: cleave the doubt born of ignorance with the sword of wisdom, take refuge in Yoga, and arise!

chapterFindings: Chapter 4 provides unbroken, one-to-one alignment for all 42 canonical references without omissions, expansions, or text loss.
The avatar declaration (4.7-4.8) and the comprehensive categorization of yajñas (4.24-4.32) are accurately segmented.
Twenty intra-line verse transitions (e.g. 4.1/4.2, 4.5-4.8, 4.10-4.13, 4.17-4.23, 4.25/4.26, 4.32-4.37, 4.39-4.42) reflect precise poetic clause divisions.
